c.v: A car crash in Warren is a Michigan no-fault claim shaped by the city’s roads. Warren is laid out on a mile-road grid from Eight Mile to Fourteen Mile, crossed by wide north-south arterials: Dequindre, Ryan, Mound, Van Dyke, Hoover, Schoenherr, and Groesbeck on the diagonal, with I-696 across the middle. The serious crashes happen where those roads meet. In 2025, according to Michigan State Police crash data, 11 Mile at Van Dyke recorded 180 crashes and one death, the second-highest count of any intersection in Michigan. Add the truck traffic serving the General Motors Technical Center, Stellantis’s Warren Truck Assembly, and the Detroit Arsenal, and a Warren crash claim usually turns on two things: who had the right of way, and how much insurance is on the other side.

sections.heading: Where Warren crashes happen, and whose road it is

c.v: Eight lanes from Eight Mile to Fourteen Mile, past the Tech Center’s east side and Warren Truck. The 11 Mile intersection is second on the state’s list.

The plant corridor, rebuilt north of I-696 in the Innovate Mound project, finished in December 2023, with new signals and turn lanes; the stretch from Eight Mile to I-696 is still awaiting funding. Tractor-trailers enter and leave the Tech Center, Warren Truck, and the Arsenal at shift changes. Turning-truck crashes at the plant gates, trucks stopped in lanes, and rear-end crashes into slowing trucks are Mound’s cases; see our

Groesbeck crosses the east side on a diagonal, producing skewed intersections with poor sight lines at the mile roads. Eight Mile is the Detroit line, where coverage on the other side of the crash is often thinner. I-696 has interchanges at Dequindre, Mound, Van Dyke, Hoover, and Schoenherr within about six miles, where merging and lane-change crashes concentrate.
The mile roads and city streets.
Nine through Fourteen Mile, Ryan, Hoover, Schoenherr, and Hayes: signal crashes, and pedestrian and bicycle crashes near schools and senior housing (see our

Van Dyke, Groesbeck, Eight Mile, and I-696 are MDOT’s; a road-defect claim against MDOT goes to the Court of Claims, with written notice filed there within 120 days (MCL 691.1404). Mound and many of the mile roads, such as 10 Mile and 14 Mile, are the Macomb County Department of Roads'; other streets are the City of Warren’s, and the City’s Engineering Division confirms which agency has a given street. A pothole or other defect in the roadbed can make the agency a defendant alongside the other driver; on State and county roads, signals, signs, and sight obstructions generally fall outside the highway exception. Notice to the wrong agency is not notice.

In a rear-end crash, fault is rarely disputed. In a left-turn or signal crash at a Warren intersection, it is disputed often, and the other driver’s insurer may try to assign you half or more of the fault. That number matters: if you are found more than 50 percent at fault, you lose your claim for pain and suffering, and below that your recovery is reduced by your share (MCL 500.3135(2)(b)). At exactly 50 percent you recover half. The evidence that decides it is perishable:

sections.heading: Who pays after a Warren crash

c.v: Your own auto insurer pays your medical expenses up to the PIP level you chose, 85 percent of lost wages for up to three years up to the monthly cap DIFS sets each October, replacement services at $20 a day, and attendant care, regardless of fault (MCL 500.3107). If you have no policy, a resident relative’s policy pays (MCL 500.3114); if none exists, the Michigan Assigned Claims Plan does (MCL 500.3172), capped at $250,000 for medical benefits. The insurer must receive written notice within one year (MCL 500.3145(1)) and must pay each bill within 30 days of reasonable proof or owe 12 percent interest (MCL 500.3142). See our
Your claim against the at-fault driver.

For pain and suffering, you need a threshold injury: death, serious impairment of body function, or permanent serious disfigurement (MCL 500.3135(1)). A serious impairment is an objectively manifested impairment of an important body function that affects your general ability to lead your normal life; it does not have to be permanent (MCL 500.3135(5);

, 2010). You can also recover lost wages beyond the three years and medical bills above your chosen PIP level (MCL 500.3135(3)(c)). The suit must be filed within three years (MCL 600.5805(2)). The mini tort recovers up to $3,000 in vehicle damage not covered by your policy (MCL 500.3135(3)(e)), filed in the 37th District Court if the insurer will not pay it.

A crash caused by a drunk driver adds a claim against the bar or store that served a visibly intoxicated person or a minor. Written notice must go to the retailer within 120 days after you hire a lawyer, the drunk driver must be named and kept in the suit, and the suit must be filed within two years, not three (MCL 436.1801(3), (4)). faqs.question: How dangerous is Van Dyke in Warren?

answer.v: 11 Mile at Van Dyke recorded 180 crashes and one death in 2025, the second-highest count of any intersection in Michigan according to the Michigan State Police. First was 18½ Mile at Van Dyke in Sterling Heights, with 210.

faqs.question: How many car accidents happen in Warren each year?

answer.v: Warren recorded 4,086 crashes, 1,261 injuries, and 13 deaths in 2024. Macomb County as a whole recorded 21,960 crashes, 6,596 injuries, and 70 deaths in 2024.

faqs.question: The other driver’s insurer says I was half at fault for a left turn on Van Dyke. Is my claim over?

answer.v: No. You lose the pain-and-suffering claim only if you are found more than 50 percent at fault. At 50 percent you recover half. The diagram, the signal data, the cameras, and the witnesses decide the number, not the adjuster.

faqs.question: I was hit by a truck turning into a plant on Mound. Who is responsible?

answer.v: The driver and the carrier, and possibly the plant or its logistics contractor if the gate layout or traffic control contributed. The preservation letter goes to all of them.

faqs.question: The driver who hit me had no insurance. What now?

answer.v: Your no-fault benefits are unaffected: your own insurer, a household member’s, or the Assigned Claims Plan pays your medical bills and lost wages. Your pain-and-suffering claim depends on your uninsured motorist coverage.

faqs.question: Where would my Warren case be filed?

answer.v: Mini tort and claims up to $25,000 in the 37th District Court on Common Road; injury suits over $25,000 in the Sixteenth Judicial Circuit Court in Mount Clemens.
One year to give your no-fault insurer written notice, three years to sue the at-fault driver, two years to sue a bar, and 120 days for a notice to the City or the Department of Roads.
